operations.comment: ; bank00.asm: PRG bank 00 (8 KiB)
; Sound engine (mapped by SoundUpdate in the NMI with SetPrgBankNoSave).
; Entry points: SndInit ($8784), SndStart ($818B, id in SoundStartId) and
; SndTick ($8184, once per frame).  Ids $00-$1F are music, $20-$3F sound
; effects, $80+ toggles (pauses) the music.
; Channel records are 9 bytes, indexed by X: music channels X = 0, 9, 18, 27
; (square 1, square 2, triangle, noise); effect channels X = $28 (square 2)
; and $31 (noise) use the same field layout at $042E+.  SndCount ($FE)
; counts channels down (4..1), so (4 - SndCount)*4 is the APU register base.
; SndStatus: bits 0-3 music channel active, bit 4 effect on square 2,
; bit 5 effect on noise, bit 6 effect playing, bit 7 music playing.
; Referenced from: SndCmd2_Note, SndCmd5_Length, SndEnvelopeStep, SndProcessChannels, SndStart
; Volume envelopes: 16-byte rows of volume steps, $FF ends a row.  Row
; chosen by command $Ex (SndEnvIndex = x*16), stepped by SndEnvelopeStep.
; Note period tables (16-bit APU timer values) for note numbers 0-15; the
; second table is used when the note byte has bit 7 set.  The period is
; shifted right SndChOctave times.  SndNoteLengthTable: 32 note lengths in
; frames (commands $5x and $6x).  SndCommandTable: handler per command high
; nibble ($1x shares SndCmd0_End, $6x SndCmd5_Length, $Dx SndCmd2_Note).
; SndTablePtrs: pointers to the music and effect tables.
; Per-frame tick: music channels, then effect channels.
; Start sound SoundStartId.  $00-$1F: music (SndStartMusic); $80+: toggle
; music pause (SndToggleMusicPause); $20-$3F: effect - header from the effect
; table.  Effect $39 is only accepted while effect $3A is playing; while an
; effect plays, a new one replaces it only if its priority byte is not lower.
; Effect header: priority byte, then two channel pointers (square 2, noise).
; Music header: tempo byte, then four channel pointers.  All four music
; channels start with a 1-frame timer; loop/envelope state is cleared.
; Silence the four music channels and flip SndStatus bit 7 (music on/off).
; Count the tempo divider; on expiry process the four music channels.
; Channel loop (X = record offset, SndChanBit, SndCount).  An inactive
; channel is skipped; a running note only updates its envelope/vibrato
; (SndUpdateEnvelope); when the timer expires the next sequence command is
; executed (SndNextCommand).
; Read the command byte at SndDataPtr and jump to SndCommandTable[byte>>4].
; Handlers return through SndAdvancePtr or loop back here.
; Effect pass skips one record (effects use square 2 and noise only).
; Command $0x/$1x: end of channel data.  Music: clear the channel bit; when
; all music channels have ended, a nonzero byte chains to that music id,
; zero stops the music.  Effects: hand the channel back to the music
; settings (SndSq2Ctrl/SndNoiseCtrl) and stop the effect when both channels ended.
; Command $2x/$Dx: play a note.  Restarts the volume envelope, then writes
; period and length.  The noise channel takes the period from the low nibble
; (SndWriteNoise); tonal channels look up SndPeriodTable/Alt.
; Command $3x: set the octave shift to x (not used on noise).
; Command $4x: rest - restart the note timer and silence the channel.
; Commands $5x/$6x: note length from SndNoteLengthTable (x or x+16).
; Command $7x: restart the timer; $77 just holds, other values retrigger the
; current note.  Exact use is inferred.
; Command $8x: set constant volume x and stop this channel's envelope.
; Command $9x: duty cycle bits (square) or the triangle control value.
; Command $Ax: repeat blocks with two nesting levels.  Bits 0/2 select the
; loop start (next byte = repeat count, pointer saved in SndLoopPtr), bits
; 1/3 the loop end (decrement and jump back while the count is nonzero).
; Command $Bx: note x with the next byte as sweep register value.
; For the square channels write $08 (sweep disabled) and silence it.
; Command $Cx: write the following byte (OR $80) to the sweep register.
; Command $Ex: select volume envelope x and start it.
; While a note sounds: advance its envelope (SndEnvelopeStep) or vibrato
; (SndUpdateVibrato).
; Write the next envelope volume; $FF (high nibble set) ends the envelope.
; Command $Fx: vibrato setup for tonal channels: bit 3 off, bits 0-2 depth
; and speed (stored in SndVibDepth / SndVibState).
; Oscillate the period low byte around the note by the vibrato step,
; reversing direction (bit 6) at the depth limit.
; Process the two effect channels (X = $28, SndCount 3 and 1).
; SND_CHN |= channel bit (register offset $15 = $4015).
; Write SndArg to APU register (4 - SndCount)*4 + SndRegOffset.  Music writes
; to a channel currently owned by an effect are dropped.  Writes to $4015
; also update SndChnShadow.
; Stop everything: clear SndChnShadow, stop music and effects.
; Silence all music channels, clear the channel bits and zero every APU
; register; sweeps disabled ($08).
; ---- Data: physical $007F7..$0080F, bank 00 $87E7-$87FE (24 bytes)
; Referenced from: SndTablePtrs
; Music table (32 words, ids $00-$1F; 0 = unused id), pointed at by
; SndTablePtrs and indexed by SndStartMusic.
; Each entry points at a header: tempo byte then four channel pointers.
; ---- Data: physical $0080F..$02010, bank 00 $87FF-$9FFF (6145 bytes)
; Referenced from: SndTablePtrs, SoundUpdate
; Effect table (32 words, ids $20-$3F) pointing at effect headers in $9Cxx.
; Music and effect data, one labelled chunk per id (MusicNN = music id NN,
; SfxNN = effect id NN, from SndMusicTable/SndEffectTable).  Each chunk
; starts with its header followed by the channel command streams (format:
; see the SndCommandTable handlers):
;   music header:  tempo byte, then 4 stream pointers (square 1, square 2,
;                  triangle, noise)
;   effect header: priority byte (SndEffectPriority), then 2 stream pointers
;                  (square 2, noise)
; Which id plays in which situation follows from the QueueSound callers
; (e.g. $30 run scored, $2E ball, $3A deep fly); musical content is not
; transcribed.
; One byte per request id: SoundUpdate only starts ids whose byte is nonzero
; (the rest of the bank after $9F1C, 228 bytes).
; bank01.asm: PRG bank 01 (8 KiB)
; Upper half of PRG value 0 (mapped together with the bank 0 sound engine).
; Holds the umpire placement, a 4x4 sprite portrait drawer, the SNK logo and
; title/attract states (MainState 0, 1, 12, 13), the computer opponent's
; pitching, batting and manager logic, and ball-flight tables used by the
; fixed bank (BallLaunchAngleTable/BallLaunchAngleTable2).
; The computer-control routines write simulated button bits into
; SideJoyHeld/SideJoyPressed for the team flagged in TeamIsCpu.
; ---- Data: physical $02010..$0208B, bank 01 $A000-$A07A (123 bytes)
; Referenced from: PlaceUmpire
; Umpire placement tables: UmpireZoneGrid (80 bytes, 4-bit zone per screen
; region, two per byte), UmpireSpots (8 x X lo/hi, Y lo/hi), UmpireSpotPose,
; UmpireCallTimes (frames a call pose is held, by call id).
; ---- Code: physical $0208B..$0226B, bank 01 $A07B-$A25A (480 bytes)
; Place object 13 at the umpire spot for the region under the screen centre
; (scroll + $78), using UmpireZoneGrid.  A pending call in ObjTargetXLo+13 (set by
; ShowCallOverlay) becomes the pose (ObjTimer+13) for UmpireCallTimes frames.
; Object 13 is read as the umpire because its pose follows the OUT/SAFE/FOUL
; call; this is inferred.
; Far-call target (FF80 offset 24): DrawPortrait for Tmp00, then restore the
; caller's bank.
; Draw a 4x4 sprite face/portrait for id A (MenuTeam) at OAM $B4 with CHR bank
; $18 (or $14 for ids $04-$1F), tile list from PortraitData.  Ids $20+ also
; get four digit sprites from the record's two BCD bytes ($0564-$0567).
; What the ids index (players vs. teams) is not established.
; Place one digit (2 tiles from the digit table at ScreenPtrB) as sprites and advance
; the table pointer.
; ---- Data: physical $0226B..$02713, bank 01 $A25B-$A702 (1192 bytes)
; Referenced from: DrawPortrait
; Generic data $A25B-$A4EA (656 bytes): tile lists referenced through the
; PortraitData header pointers (e.g. $A25B), 16 tiles per portrait.
; Portrait header: words for the tile-list base ($A26B), digit tile table
; ($A25B), BCD record base, then attribute bytes per sprite; data follows.
; MainState 12 (first state after reset): fill both nametables with tile
; $35, draw the SNK logo from two inline PPU lists, black out the palette
; and advance to state 13.
; Inline PPU write list for PpuBufAppendInline: address hi/lo, tiles, $FE = new address, $FF = end.
; Inline PPU write list for PpuBufAppendInline: address hi/lo, tiles, $FE = new address, $FF = end.
; ---- Code: physical $02759..$027AF, bank 01 $A749-$A79E (86 bytes)
; MainState 13: step through 8 four-colour logo palettes (LogoPalettes) with
; per-step durations (LogoFadeTimes); after step 8 the screen scrolls away
; ($FF) and from step $11 - or on START - the title (state 0) begins.
; ---- Data: physical $027AF..$027BF, bank 01 $A79F-$A7AE (16 bytes)
; Referenced from: State13_LogoFade
; $A79F-$A7AE (16 bytes) read by State13_LogoFade as frame counts per fade
; ---- Code: physical $027BF..$027EC, bank 01 $A7AF-$A7DB (45 bytes)
; With rendering off, fill $2400 and $2000 with tile $35 (960 bytes) and a
; zero attribute table.
; ---- Data: physical $027EC..$0280C, bank 01 $A7DC-$A7FB (32 bytes)
; Referenced from: State13_LogoFade
; $A7DC-$A7FB (32 bytes): eight 4-byte background palettes used by
; State13_LogoFade.
; ---- Code: physical $0280C..$02850, bank 01 $A7FC-$A83F (68 bytes)
; MainState 0: title screen.  Start title music (1), reset demo and pause
; state, load palettes 2/$82, draw the two title screens with
; FarLoadScreenInline (6 inline bytes each) and a sprite-0 split marker,
; then go to state 1 with a 180-frame timer.
; far call -> FarLoadScreenInline (bank 14)
; 6 inline argument bytes consumed by far-call target FarLoadScreenInline.
; ---- Code: physical $02856..$0285F, bank 01 $A846-$A84E (9 bytes)
; far call -> FarLoadScreenInline (bank 14)
; ---- Data: physical $0285F..$02865, bank 01 $A84F-$A854 (6 bytes)
; 6 inline argument bytes consumed by far-call target FarLoadScreenInline.
; ---- Code: physical $02865..$028F9, bank 01 $A855-$A8E8 (148 bytes)
; Place the sprite-0 marker, select CHR bank $17 and split mode 1 for the
; scrolling title, then go to state 1 with a 180-frame timer.
; MainState 1: START goes to the game menus (state 6).  Otherwise every 180
; frames the lower screen scrolls by a page; after 10 pages an attract demo
; starts: random teams, both teams computer-controlled, ReturnToTitlePending
; set, MainState 8.
; ---- Data: physical $028F9..$02A36, bank 01 $A8E9-$AA25 (317 bytes)
; Title-screen graphics data used by FarLoadScreenInline from State0_Title
; and Title_LoadSecondScreen (inline words: metatile set $A8E9, maps $ACE9
; and $AE29):
;   $A8E9-$ACE8  TitleMetatiles: four 256-byte corner tables (top-left,
;                top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right tile per metatile)
;   $ACE9-$AE28  TitleMapA (nametable $2000), $AE29-$AF68 TitleMapB ($2400):
;                320-byte maps = 240 metatile ids, 16 unused, 64 attributes
; $AA26-$AA42 (a separate data region) lies inside the second corner table.
; ---- Data: physical $02A36..$02A53, bank 01 $AA26-$AA42 (29 bytes)
; $AA26-$AA42 (29 bytes): tile-code bytes ($20 blanks, $Cx-$Ex) inside
; TitleMetatiles (second corner table, $A9E9-$AAE8).
; ---- Data: physical $02A53..$02F79, bank 01 $AA43-$AF68 (1318 bytes)
; Rest of TitleMetatiles (to $ACE8), then the two title screen maps.
; ---- Code: physical $02F79..$02F8E, bank 01 $AF69-$AF7D (21 bytes)
; Computer pitching for the fielding team (when TeamIsCpu bit 7): clear its
; pad bits and dispatch on AtBatPhase.  Phase 0 plans and throws the pitch,
; phase 1 holds the first curve direction, phases 2-3 steer the ball while it
; travels (CpuSteerPitch), phase 4 does nothing.
; ---- Data: physical $02F8E..$02F98, bank 01 $AF7E-$AF87 (10 bytes)
; Jump table for JumpTableAfterJsr (entry = A); the JSR never returns here.
; ---- Code: physical $02F98..$02F9F, bank 01 $AF88-$AF8E (7 bytes)
; Sub-step ControlStep: plan, wait, walk to the plate position, then throw.
; ---- Data: physical $02F9F..$02FA7, bank 01 $AF8F-$AF96 (8 bytes)
; Jump table for JumpTableAfterJsr (entry = A); the JSR never returns here.
; ---- Code: physical $02FA7..$03034, bank 01 $AF97-$B023 (141 bytes)
; Pick a pitch plan from count-dependent tables (index Strikes*4+Balls):
; CpuPitchStrike (probably a fast/strike flag), CpuPitchSpot start position, $0521-$0523
; curve directions.  Left-right bits are mirrored when PitcherType is negative
; (probably a left-handed batter).  CpuPitchWait = random wait.
; ---- Data: physical $03034..$0308C, bank 01 $B024-$B07B (88 bytes)
; Referenced from: CpuPlanPitch
; Pitch-plan tables indexed by count (Strikes*4+Balls) and random bits.
; ---- Code: physical $0308C..$030B1, bank 01 $B07C-$B0A0 (37 bytes)
; Walk the pitcher (object 0) left/right until ObjXLo matches the planned
; spot from CpuPitchSpots, then start another wait.
; ---- Data: physical $030B1..$030B9, bank 01 $B0A1-$B0A8 (8 bytes)
; Referenced from: CpuPitch_Position
; $B0A1-$B0A8 (8 bytes): pitcher X positions ($78-$87) for the
; planned start spot (CpuPitchSpot); read by CpuPitch_Position.
; ---- Code: physical $030B9..$03121, bank 01 $B0A9-$B110 (104 bytes)
; Every 32 frames, for each runner object with ObjRunState+9 set, a 1-in-256 roll
; presses B (probably a pick-off throw).
; Steer by ball depth BallPosY+1: $60-$8F uses curve 2; past $90 either curve 3 or,
; for a strike plan (CpuPitchStrike) outside the zone, push back towards the centre.
; Referenced from: ComputeBallLanding, ComputeBallLandingFrom, CpuPlanPitch
; Pitch plans: two bytes of nibbles each (start spot, curve 1, curve 2,
; curve 3), 128 plans = 256 bytes indexed by (FrameCounter & $3E) | random
; bits from CpuPitchPlanIndex.  The rest of this block up to $B408 holds the
; fielder formation tables read by bank 15 (see below); BallLaunchAngleTable
; ($B409, 256+128 bytes) is read by ComputeBallLanding in the fixed bank.
; Deep-ball formations: 160 bytes = 10 rows of 16, indexed by a coarse
; BallY row (high nibble) and BallX column of the predicted landing point;
; each byte is a formation number 0-$0D for LoadFielderFormation
; (AssignFieldersDeepBall, with banks 0/1 mapped by FieldSetupObjects).
; Short-ball formations: 128 bytes indexed by BallDirection/2; formation
; numbers $0E-$15 (AssignFieldersShortBall).
; Fielder formations: 24 records of 9 bytes ($B331-$B408), one initial
; ObjState value per fielder object 0-8.  The fixed-bank word
; FielderPosTableBase ($DE31) holds $B331; LoadFielderFormation copies record
; 9*A.  Values are fielder state ids as dispatched by FielderStateDispatch
; (values with bit 7 set also occur; their per-state meaning is not decoded here).
; Computer manager between at-bats: try a pitching change, a pinch runner,
; a defensive change and a pinch hitter in turn; stop at the first that sets
; SubstitutionPending.  The pending change is described in
; BaseRunners+1 (type), +2 (player out) and +3 (player in).  Decision
; meanings are read from the rating/score/inning comparisons.
; For a computer fielding team: compare a fatigue score (CpuPitcherFatigue)
; against a threshold from the team table; late in the game (HalfInning >= 20)
; pick a reliever from the bullpen list, otherwise from the scheduled order.
; Referenced from: CpuConsiderPitchingChange
; $B669-$B671 (9 bytes): fatigue threshold adjustments by batting
; order position, read by CpuConsiderPitchingChange.
; Ptr16+1 = 1 when team X is not behind; scan the LineupStatus entries for a
; free bench slot.  Returns nonzero (A=1) when none is available.
; Point Ptr04 at the team's record in CpuTeamTable and Ptr0C at the pitcher's
; 4-byte threshold entry; Tmp08 = threshold for leading/trailing.
; Tmp00 = batter ratings/8 + pitcher's WRAM stat (PitcherRunsAllowed) + runner-state
; bias (CpuRunnerBias), +1/+3 more when stamina (PitcherStamina) is exhausted.
; Referenced from: CpuConsiderPinchHitterStrong, CpuPitcherFatigue
; $B701-$B708 (8 bytes): bias by base occupancy (BaseOccupancy/2), read by
; CpuPitcherFatigue and CpuConsiderPinchHitter.
; ---- Code: physical $03719..$039AA, bank 01 $B709-$B999 (657 bytes)
; For a computer batting team whose pitcher is due up (BatterSlot = pitcher
; slot): choose a pinch hitter from the bench (late innings) or keep him;
; sets CpuPinchPlayer to the incoming player.  Also counts CpuPinchDeclined.
; Built-in teams only (TeamForSide < 8).  Late and leading by 2+, swap in a
; defensive player (flag bit 5) for a weaker one (bit 1); otherwise replace a
; player whose flag bit 3 is set by a bench player with the same flag.
; Flag meanings in the team table are not established.
; Built-in computer batting team: late and within one run, put in a fast
; bench player (flag bit 4) for a slow runner on base (flag bit 0).
; If the runner on the base in Y is flagged slow (bit 0), queue a pinch-runner
; change (type 3) for him.
; From inning 3 on, a batter flagged weak (bit 2) may be pinch-hit for
; depending on score difference and base occupancy.
; ---- Data: physical $039AA..$03BA6, bank 01 $B99A-$BB95 (508 bytes)
; Referenced from: CpuLoadTeamThresholds, CpuTeamFlagsPtr
; CpuThresholdTable (14 words) and CpuTeamTable (word per team + per-player

; ---- Code: physical $03BA6..$03D39, bank 01 $BB96-$BD28 (403 bytes)
; Computer batting for the batting team.  Before the pitch, mirrors the
; close-up control (ObjTimer+9).  During the pitch, swings (A) when the predicted
; ball position (CpuPredictBallX) reaches the hitting zone, bunts (D-pad +
; A) or steals (CpuStealPlan) according to the plans made by CpuBatterPlan.
; With probability by rating BatterRatingA, move the batter left/right toward the
; ball's predicted X when it reaches the batter's Y.
; Carry clear when the ball's projected position is inside the window chosen
; by CpuSwingWindowA/CpuSwingWindowB (CpuSwingWindow tables).
; ---- Data: physical $03D39..$03D69, bank 01 $BD29-$BD58 (48 bytes)
; Referenced from: CpuBatterControl, CpuInSwingWindow
; Swing timing windows (indexed by CpuSwingWindowA/CpuSwingWindowB) and 16 random timing
; offsets (CpuSwingJitter).
; ---- Code: physical $03D69..$03DCC, bank 01 $BD59-$BDBB (99 bytes)
; Before each pitch for a computer batting team: plan steals, bunts and swing
; timing.
; With runners in steal positions (BaseOccupancy = $02 or $0A) and a fast runner,
; choose a steal type (CpuStealPlan) from count tables.
; ---- Data: physical $03DCC..$03DFC, bank 01 $BDBC-$BDEB (48 bytes)
; Referenced from: CpuPlanSteal
; ---- Code: physical $03DFC..$03E83, bank 01 $BDEC-$BE72 (135 bytes)
; With fewer than 2 outs and 2 strikes, runners on and no runner on 3rd, a weak batter
; (BatterRatingA+BatterRatingB below a random roll) bunts (CpuBatPlan = 2), sometimes squeeze (3).
; Choose the swing timing windows CpuSwingWindowA/CpuSwingWindowB from count tables (weaker

; ---- Data: physical $03E83..$04010, bank 01 $BE73-$BFFF (397 bytes)
; Referenced from: CpuPlanSwingTiming
; CpuSwingTimingB (32 bytes) is followed by $FF fill to the end of the bank

; bank02.asm: PRG bank 02 (8 KiB)
; Lower half of PRG value 1 (with bank 3).  Contains the in-game lineup /
; substitution menus (pinch hitter, relief pitcher, pinch runner, defensive

; set in bank 8: $20 blanks, rising tile codes, $88 fill at the end of each
; page).  No reader was identified, so this reading is tentative.  Screen
; maps follow from $8400 (see ScreenMapMainMenu).
; $8143-$8165 (35 bytes): tile-code bytes ($42-$98) inside the second 256-byte
; table of the probable metatile set at $8000; classified as data with the
